findings.title: The hurt cue points the wrong way: bearing taken from a contact point on the player's own hurtbox
findings.detail: FirstPersonCamera.hit_bearing() measures the contact point against the lens. It falls back to the push direction only when the contact is within HURT_SIDE_MIN_M (0.05 m) horizontally. Real contacts are on the hurtbox surface (hit_detector.gd:197), 0.1-0.33 m from the lens and often behind it, so the bearing is close to noise. The overlay's strokes and the camera's roll both use this bearing. Probe of all 9 hurt-act hits ('PROBE' print in on_player_hit): Punk jab from the front 0 deg (right); Punk jab from the left -144 / -140 deg (reads as behind); Kicker jump kick from the front -86 deg (strokes on the LEFT edge); Kicker from the left -150 deg; Bruiser smash from the front +121 deg (strokes on the RIGHT and bottom, and a roll as if struck from the right); Bruiser from the left -101 deg (right). In the burst probe, a Thug straight ahead hits at -125, +164 and -141 deg, so all three show bottom strokes, as if from behind. hit.direction (the push) is correct in every case: z+ for front hits, x+ for left hits. Game-boy's check 'it says where the hit came from' fails for most frontal hits. In a crowd, nearly every hit lights the bottom edge. The unit tests pass only because they put the contact 0.4 m out along the attack direction (tests/test_m6_feedback_feel.gd:81), which real hits never do.
findings.evidence: Stills: front_wrong.png (hurt/bot.avi f275 Punk from the left: bottom and left strokes; f625 Kicker straight ahead: left-edge strokes; f1083 Bruiser straight ahead: right-edge strokes). hurt_sheet.png row 2 (left jab: bottom strokes). Probe log /Users/arachne/repos/beat-em-up-PoC/.worktrees/m6-review-feedback-world/captures/review/hurt_probe/bot.log, e.g. 'HURT kicker jump kick front / PROBE bearing -86.2 local (-0.116, -0.194, -0.008) dir (0, -0.10, 0.99)' and 'HURT bruiser smash front / PROBE bearing 120.8 local (0.142, -0.136, 0.085)'. Burst probe: captures/review/burst/bot.log, Thug1 bearings -124.6 / 164.3 / -141.4. Code: game/camera/first_person_camera.gd:823-827.
findings.repro: In the review worktree, add a print of rad_to_deg(bearing) in HurtOverlay.on_player_hit and run tools/capture_bot.sh res://tests/bot/crowd_bot.tscn captures/review/hurt_probe "Look: player hurt". Or watch 'Look: player hurt' at f623 (Kicker straight ahead) and f1080 (Bruiser straight ahead): the strokes are on the side and bottom edges, not the top.
findings.suggested_fix: In hit_bearing(), use the attacker's position against the view as the primary bearing (hit.attacker.global_position), with -hit.direction as the fallback. Or use the contact only when it is more than about 0.5 m from the lens. Add a test that takes a real hit from HitDetector (a Punk at 1 m to the left, a Kicker straight ahead) and checks which edge and roll sign result. Move HURT_SIDE_MIN_M into Tuning (see the low finding).

skeptic.reason: Confirmed. The probe log shows real contacts 0.1-0.33 m from the lens, with bearings that disagree with the attacker side. FB-FEEL's call 4 and fix-feedback.md line 58 intend the overlay to say where the hit came from, and a fix does not change the spec. It only changes the source of the bearing.
skeptic.evidence: The probe log (captures/review/hurt_probe/bot.log) has real hits with `PROBE bearing -86.2 local (-0.116,-0.194,-0.008) dir (0,-0.10,0.99)` for a Kicker straight ahead, `120.8` for a Bruiser straight ahead, and `-143.8` / `-139.5` for a Punk jab from the left, where the push dir is +x. The contact is `center + (sample-center).limit_length(radius)` (hit_detector.gd:197), so it sits on the player's own hurtbox, within about 0.35 m of the lens. A hurtbox centre offset from the eye by 0.1-0.3 m pushes it past the 0.05 m threshold in hit_bearing (first_person_camera.gd:823-827), so the fallback to the push direction never fires. `hit.direction` is the attacker-to-victim horizontal radial (hit_detector.gd:~200), so it is accurate. The unit-test helper (tests/test_m6_feedback_feel.gd:~75-82) puts the contact 0.4 m out along the attack direction, which real hits never do, so the tests pass anyway.
skeptic.root_cause: hit_bearing() reads hit.contact_point against the lens. For hits on the player that point lies on the player's own hurtbox surface, a few tenths of a metre from the camera and often behind it, so the bearing is nearly random. The push-direction fallback only triggers within 0.05 m, which essentially never happens. Both the overlay strokes (hurt_overlay.gd:105) and the camera roll (_roll_away) use this bearing.

The boss roof Ground (200 m, top -0.5 in world coordinates) shares its top with three 75 m accent strips in the roofs section, so the same flashing returns on the boss roof gap-down view. The coplanar test misses these strips because it only looks at ground-like modules. This is a real defect, not an approved departure.

findings.title: No recording shows a finisher, or unblocked crowd hits, landing on the player
findings.detail: The brief's hurt act asks for a Punk, a Kicker and a Bruiser to land a light, a heavy and a finisher each, from three sides. look_hurt_acts.gd's ATTACKS throws one attack per archetype (index 0): the Punk jab and cross (LIGHT), the Kicker jump kick (LIGHT) and the Bruiser smash (HEAVY). No FINISHER-tier hit is ever taken, so the 7-degree finisher roll (hurt_roll_finisher_deg), the trauma cap of 1.0 and the overlay's full strength are never seen in first person. 'Mixed six, fight' and 'Run: held back' run in god mode: every hit taken is 0 dmg and mostly PERFECT (parried), so the panel jolt and a real crowd burst are absent from them too. Three of the brief's checks are unjudged by this round's recordings: 'not nauseating in a crowd (several hits in a row, the 7-degree finisher roll)', 'blocked hits still feel as in M6', and 'unmistakable from the side and behind' at heavy and finisher tiers. My burst probe (6 light hits in 66 frames, 100 to 50 HP) was not nauseating. It had no finisher either: the Thug's index-0 chain landed three LIGHT hits.
findings.evidence: hurt/bot.log: HURT-HIT tiers are LIGHT x7 and HEAVY x3, no FINISHER. fight/bot.log and run_street/bot.log: every 'Player:' line is '0.0 dmg', 11 of 13 PERFECT. tests/bot/acts/look_hurt_acts.gd ATTACKS (3 entries, all index 0). Probe burst: /Users/arachne/repos/beat-em-up-PoC/.worktrees/m6-review-feedback-world/captures/review/burst/bot.avi, burst_sheet.png.
findings.suggested_fix: Extend ATTACKS in tests/bot/acts/look_hurt_acts.gd with a finisher-tier attack: the Thug's or Ox's chain that ends in pipe_swing_3 or chain_swing_3 (FINISHER in tools/gen_moves.gd), or a Punk Shove. Add a blocked case and a 3-attacker burst with real damage. Re-record and judge the roll and nausea from a 12 fps sheet.

skeptic.reason: Confirmed. The brief (fix-feedback.md line 68) asks that a Punk, Kicker and Bruiser each land a light, a heavy and a finisher on the standing player from front, left and behind. The act throws only one index-0 attack per archetype, so no FINISHER-tier hit is ever recorded. This is a recording/coverage gap in the act, not a game defect, and it is not a ruled departure or a logged call.
skeptic.evidence: tests/bot/acts/look_hurt_acts.gd lines 12-16: ATTACKS has 3 entries (punk jab, kicker jump kick, bruiser smash), all index 0. captures/m6-feedback-review/hurt/bot.log has 24 HURT-HIT lines: 18 LIGHT (12 at 6, 6 at 8) and 6 HEAVY at 15; 0 FINISHER. captures/m6-feedback-review/fight/bot.log 'Player:' lines are all '0.0 dmg' (god mode), mostly PERFECT. FINISHER-tier moves exist in tools/gen_moves.gd (uppercut, shove, haymaker, spinning_heel, stomp_kick, push_kick, pipe_swing_3, chain_swing_3), so a finisher can be thrown by an attacker.
skeptic.root_cause: look_hurt_acts.gd's ATTACKS table holds a single index-0 attack per archetype, and the act never exercises a finisher, a blocked hit or a multi-attacker burst with real damage. Unjudged are the 7-degree finisher roll, the trauma cap, the full overlay, blocked-hit feel and nausea in a crowd. Fight and run_street cover none of this because they run in god mode with PERFECT parries.

findings.title: Hurt feel thresholds are script constants
findings.detail: HURT_SIDE_MIN_M (0.05 m) and HURT_FRONTAL_SINE (0.1) decide which side a hit reads from and when it counts as frontal (the half-roll to alternating sides). Those are feel numbers. CLAUDE.md says feel numbers are never script constants and belong in Tuning ('Hit feel > Hurt'). HURT_SIDE_MIN_M is also the threshold behind the high finding.
findings.suggested_fix: Move both into tuning_data.gd's Hit feel > Hurt subgroup as @export_range values with ## docs (or remove HURT_SIDE_MIN_M when the bearing comes from the attacker), then regenerate tuning/default.json.

findings.title: The ground's tone patches read a little camouflage-like and darker than the mood board; the 8 m grates repeat visibly
findings.detail: Against mood_street_a.jpg (broad, pale, warm washes with sparse ink), the street floor is a dark blue-grey covered in many lumpy flat blobs of 2-3 values, mostly without outlines, so it reads busy, close to camouflage. It reads better than M6's noise but not like the concept's open ground. In the A2 walk of the drift, a drain grate and a manhole appear at the same spot in every 8 m tile, so the repeat shows when you look down the street. This is taste, not a defect: it does not flicker.
findings.evidence: drift6.png (drift/bot.avi f40, f300, f500, f700, f950, f1150): blob patches across the whole floor, with grates at a regular spacing in the bottom row. cmp_mood.png (mood board beside tour f100).
findings.repro: Watch 'Look: ground drift' a2 walk (f1039-1218), or view tour pose 0 street_start.
findings.suggested_fix: In tools/gen_trim.gd's ground tile, use fewer and larger tone patches and lift the base value toward the mood's pale asphalt (the ground.hsv band in trim_layout.json). Give a few patches an ink outline. Vary the manhole and grate placement between tiles (for example a 16 m pattern, or offsets by world cell). Then rerun gen_trim.gd --check.

findings.title: Hurt feel numbers are script literals, against the 'feel numbers are never script constants' rule
findings.detail: HurtOverlay hardcodes the vignette's gradient stops (0.4 of depth, 0.4 alpha), the stroke geometry (0.55 + 0.7 length, 0.4/count half-width, +-0.6 lean, +-0.3 jitter, strength*1.5, +0.3), the top-stroke threshold (cos-0.5)*2, and the blocked-depth factor feel*2.0. PlayerHealthPanel.jolt_offset hardcodes the rattle frequencies 95 and 113. The camera adds two script constants, HURT_SIDE_MIN_M and HURT_FRONTAL_SINE. These shape what the player feels and are not reachable from the Tuning panel, though the other hurt_* values are. Game-boy cannot tune the stroke length or the jolt rate without a code edit.
findings.repro: grep the literals in the listed lines. Open Tuning > Hit feel > Hurt: there is no row for stroke length, the gradient falloff or the jolt frequency.
findings.suggested_fix: Move the stroke length range, the gradient mid-stop and the jolt frequency into the Hurt subgroup as @export_range values (for example hurt_overlay_stroke_len_min/max, hurt_overlay_mid_stop, hurt_panel_jolt_hz). Update tuning/default.json, and the Hit feel row count in test_tuning_panel (36) moves with them.

skeptic.reason: The literals are all present as described and break the project rule that feel numbers are never script constants. No logged call or spec ruling approves them. Severity is low rather than medium: the main hurt values (colour, depth, strength, jolt px and seconds, roll degrees) are tunable, and the leftovers are shape constants.
skeptic.evidence: Read at 82bab12. game/ui/hurt_overlay.gd: gradient mid-stop uses 0.4 for both depth and alpha (~lines 180-186). Stroke geometry has 0.55 + randf*0.7 length, 0.4/count half-width, ±0.6 lean, ±0.3 jitter, strength*1.5 and +0.3 (~197-202). Top-stroke threshold is (cos-0.5)*2 (~112). Blocked-depth factor is feel*2.0 (~117). game/ui/player_health_panel.gd:109 has sin(_time*95), cos(_time*113). game/camera/first_person_camera.gd:88,90 define const HURT_SIDE_MIN_M=0.05 and HURT_FRONTAL_SINE=0.1. game/autoload/tuning_data.gd:215-242 has the hurt_overlay_* and hurt_panel_jolt_* exports but none for stroke length, gradient mid-stop or jolt frequency. M6-calls/FB-FEEL.md does not mention these literals as a deliberate call. HURT_SIDE_MIN_M is a degenerate-geometry epsilon and HURT_FRONTAL_SINE is a dead-zone threshold, so the camera pair is the weakest part of the finding.
skeptic.root_cause: The FB-FEEL builder exposed the headline hurt values as tunables but left shape and rhythm constants inline in the overlay draw code, the health panel and the camera.

findings.title: The Ground fix puts the far Ground's top coplanar with three drawn Skyline walkway slabs; the new guard test misses it
findings.detail: Ground (BossRoof, 200x200 m, slab_dark) now has its top at world y -0.5. Roofs/Skyline's WestWalkRoof (3.4x75 m), EastWalkRoof (2.5x75 m) and EastWalkFacade (4x75 m) are 'accent' slabs drawn with solid=false, with their tops also at y -0.5 (z -120..-45). Before the fix the Ground sat at y 0 above them, so they were hidden. A probe over all 299 drawn blocks lists these three pairs as coplanar tops. test_no_two_drawn_ground_planes_of_the_level_share_a_top filters to modules floor, slab_dark and deck, and the slabs resolve to the accent look, so it passes. A still from over the skyline (shot_b.png, crop_b2.png) shows faint banding on that surface and no visible flicker, so this is geometric, not seen moving. The skyline lane dashes (top y -0.76) stay buried under the Ground, as before the fix.
findings.evidence: game/level/mission1/boss_roof.tscn:178 (Ground y -13, height 1); game/level/mission1/roofs.tscn:1120-1139 (slabs at y -5.15, height 0.3, tops at world -0.5); probe output 'COPLANAR Skyline/WestWalkRoof vs BossRoof/Geometry/Ground 3.40x75.00 at y -0.50 top' (also EastWalkRoof 2.5x75, EastWalkFacade 4x75); tests/test_m6_feedback_ground.gd _ground_like
findings.repro: Instantiate mission1.tscn, take every LevelBlock with draw_box true, and compare world_aabb().end.y pairs within 0.01 m with an xz overlap over 0.8 m2. Then view the Skyline area from above the roofs section, for example a camera at (-7, 9, -62) looking at (-7, -0.5, -80).
findings.suggested_fix: Drop the Ground a further 0.2 m (y -13.2) or turn off draw_box on the three slabs. Widen _ground_like to any drawn block at most 1 m thick, not only three modules.

findings.title: The new strip-ink fade uses the max-axis footprint, so ink on grazing strip surfaces (roof decks, kerb tops) fades within about 6 to 10 m, not the 20 m the tunable's comment suggests
findings.detail: ink_mask() fades every non-ground trim strip by smoothstep(ink_fade.x, ink_fade.y, texels), with texels = max(length(gx), length(gy)), the larger axis. The comment says 'a wall seen square at 10 m is about 9 texels a pixel, at 20 m about 17'. That holds for walls. For a horizontal surface seen from eye height 1.6 m, the footprint along the view direction is about pixel_rad*r^2/h. With a 75 degree vertical FOV at 1080p that is about 17 texels at 6 m and about 46 at 10 m on a U-aligned 512 texel/m strip. Seam and joint ink on concrete and roof-tar decks, and kerb tops, therefore starts to fade near 6 m and is mostly gone by 10 m (about 68% faded at 10 m). The calls file (FB-GROUND item 3) sets the 16 to 64 range without a grazing case. It also affects brick, plaster and facade strips, which the repaint did not touch.
findings.evidence: game/fx/trim_body.gdshaderinc ink_mask() (non-ground branch) and the texels calculation; Tuning ground_ink_fade_start_texels 16 and ground_ink_fade_end_texels 64; docs/milestones/M6-calls/FB-GROUND.md item 3. The footprint figures are computed by hand, not measured in a recording.
findings.repro: Stand on a roof deck (roof_tar strip) and look along it. The lap seams lose their ink about 8 to 10 m away, where the near-field kerb and joint ink is bold. Compare with ground_ink_fade_start_texels raised to 64 in the Tuning panel.
findings.suggested_fix: Measure the fade by the min-axis footprint, or by the geometric mean of the two axes, or raise the defaults (for example 48 to 160) if roof decks should keep their seams to 15 m. Capture a roof-deck look act before deciding.

findings.title: The shared 'no other character' guards are now mostly vacuous, and a test file's mere existence opts a character out
findings.detail: _rolled_out(id) returns true for the Bruiser and for any character with a tests/test_m6_feedback_detail_<id>.gd. All four other enemies now have one, so test_no_other_character_uses_the_pilots_keys, test_no_other_character_uses_the_valley_or_texel_keys and the enemy half of test_no_other_mask_has_codes check nothing but the dummy and the player. That is by design, and the guards still check the player mask. The opt-out is by filename, so an empty or stale test file would disable a guard silently.
findings.repro: Run -gselect=test_m6_feedback_detail.gd: the loops skip every enemy.
findings.suggested_fix: Have _rolled_out also require that the character's pipeline.json holds the key. Alternatively, add a test that every character's per-character test file has at least one test that reads its own pipeline.json.
